test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 28 Oct, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 1.
solution:
The correct answer is '**are**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The sentence is: "There (1) _________ some firsts that stay in history forever."
 
• The subject of the verb in blank (1) is "some firsts," which is a plural noun.
 
• The phrase "that stay in history forever" indicates a general truth or ongoing state, requiring a present tense verb.
 
• Therefore, the plural present tense form of "to be," which is "**are**," is the appropriate choice.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

Complete Passage: *Khashaba Jadhav was the independent India's first individual olympic medallist. There (1) are__ some firsts that stay in history forever. The one held by Khashaba Jadhav is one such first. He might have been referred to as the Pocket Dynamo, but his deeds dwarfed those of far (2) _________ athletes in his sport. Just a couple of years after India had become a Republic, Jadhav took part in the 1952 Olympics at Helsinki, Finland. As funding sportsperson's weren't really a (3) _________ for a country just finding its feet, Jadhav’s trip to Helsinki was actually funded by the public. Jadhav however, (4) _________ his way to fame, becoming independent India's first individual Olympic medal winner. He (5) _________ bronze in the bantamweight category.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

 
• **Option 1: "is"** – This is the singular present tense form, incorrect for a plural subject.
 
• **Option 2: "was"** – This is the singular past tense form, incorrect for a plural subject and also the present tense context.
 
• **Option 3: "were"** – This is the plural past tense form. While plural, the context ("stay in history forever") implies an ongoing truth, favoring the present tense.
